bug_semantics: A remote unauthenticated attacker can submit an unlimited sequence of incorrect administrator credentials to either /j_security_check (j_password) or /management/domain (HTTP Authorization). Before the fix, each request is authenticated immediately and a failed attempt merely returns the login error/HTTP 401; no per-user/host attempt state, delay, concurrency cap, or temporary lockout makes online brute-force guessing progressively more expensive.
flaw_origin: The smallest causal origin recoverable from public history is javaee/glassfish commit 0fee8143d3ad099bb7b4583785693957c838523a (SVN r29730), which added the REST wrapper and its security path for /management/domain. RestAdapter.authenticate invokes AdminAuthenticator for every request and, on false, immediately emits 401 plus WWW-Authenticate: BASIC without retaining failed-attempt state. Its parent exposed /management/domain directly and had no authenticated failed-login path. Commit c1f1b2942b2a657eb61e707069dd4ea9d3e3a730 later expanded the same omission to the Admin Console: AdminConsoleAuthModule accepted /j_security_check credentials and posted them to REST, forwarding failure to the error page without throttling. Eclipse commit 571714739b23e16c4c90d5229b806433920b3bcb is only the 2018 Initial Contribution snapshot; following the files in the public predecessor history decomposes that aggregate to 0fee8143d3ad099bb7b4583785693957c838523a rather than treating the import or later moves as the BIC.
ai_marker: BIC commit-object check: https://api.github.com/repos/javaee/glassfish/git/commits/0fee8143d3ad099bb7b4583785693957c838523a records human author and committer Rajeshwar Patil <rajeshwar@java.net> at 2009-07-25T05:30:30Z. The complete message is 'Wrapper adapter for REST interface support...' followed by SVN revision and Former-commit-id metadata. It has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI-tool trailer, bot identity, or other AI marker.
evidence: First-party report https://gitlab.eclipse.org/security/vulnerability-reports/-/issues/231 identifies remote unauthenticated attacks against https://HOST:PORT/j_security_check using j_password and https://HOST:PORT/management/domain using Authorization, demonstrates 50 failed attempts followed by a successful 51st, and states that no special configuration is required.

The updated Eclipse CVE publication request https://gitlab.eclipse.org/security/cve-assignment/-/issues/128 gives the complete affected set: 5.1.0; 6.0.0 through 6.2.5; 7.0.0 through 7.0.25; 7.1.0; and 8.0.0 through versions before 8.0.3. It explicitly says GlassFish 8.0.3 adds automatic brute-force protection.

BIC reproduction: inspect https://api.github.com/repos/javaee/glassfish/commits/0fee8143d3ad099bb7b4583785693957c838523a. The patch adds v3/admin/rest/src/main/java/org/glassfish/admin/rest/RestAdapter.java and RestManagementAdapter.java. RestManagementAdapter exposes CONTEXT '/management' and DomainResource; RestAdapter.service calls authenticate for every request; authenticate delegates to AdminAuthenticator and, on failure, only writes 401 and WWW-Authenticate: BASIC. There is no counter, timestamp, delay, lock, or attempt tracker.

Direct-parent reproduction: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/javaee/glassfish/7975999a9bce3825ec4b162a92c1c51f00b0f4f1/v3/admin/rest/src/main/java/org/glassfish/admin/rest/RestAdapter.java is absent (404). The parent's RestService at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/javaee/glassfish/7975999a9bce3825ec4b162a92c1c51f00b0f4f1/v3/admin/rest/src/main/java/org/glassfish/admin/rest/RestService.java registers /management directly through ContainerFactory and contains no authentication/failure-handling path. The BIC patch itself reports RestAdapter as added, proving the parent lacks the vulnerable failed-login loop.

History/decomposition reproduction: the javaee/glassfish commits API for paths v3/admin/rest/src/main/java/org/glassfish/admin/rest/RestAdapter.java, then .../adapter/RestAdapter.java, then the later main/appserver and main/nucleus paths shows 0fee8143 as the original add followed by package/module moves (34270938430281786cca8234fcb5f4737f9b44b5, 356b4e21b8c290ca84b55cd159c4cdfd3d204c76, 48b5ca208cdb35b69928c4c83925fd329c86614e, b4ef8f4979da4678327d0ca66c3174a854aef7eb, 168ce449c4ea0826842ab4129e83c4a700750970). In the validated Eclipse clone, 'git log --follow -- nucleus/admin/util/src/main/java/com/sun/enterprise/admin/util/GenericAdminAuthenticator.java' stops at root snapshot 571714739b23e16c4c90d5229b806433920b3bcb, confirming why predecessor-history decomposition is necessary.

Console-path lifecycle reproduction: https://api.github.com/repos/javaee/glassfish/commits/c1f1b2942b2a657eb61e707069dd4ea9d3e3a730 shows AdminConsoleAuthModule added. validateRequest recognizes /j_security_check, reads j_username/j_password, makes an authenticated REST POST, and on rejection forwards to loginErrorPage with no failure state or delay. This is a later path expansion, not the earliest BIC.

Fix reproduction in the validated clone: 'git show 8577a9d602ad76354c3625673979038848aa3142 -- nucleus/admin/util/src/main/java/com/sun/enterprise/admin/util/AuthenticationAttemptTracker.java nucleus/admin/util/src/main/java/com/sun/enterprise/admin/util/GenericAdminAuthenticator.java appserver/admingui/common/src/main/java/org/glassfish/admingui/common/security/AdminConsoleAuthModule.java' shows the new shared tracker, pre-auth rejection, success reset, and failure recording with exponential 2^(failures-1)-second delay capped at 60 seconds and a three-concurrent-delay cap producing TooManyRequestsException. The later commits in the same PR refine proxy host handling and map growth; merge commit 6cab4ce3aad9bc65b52bc761a4aa88634a2bd0aa closes PR #26026.

Release-boundary reproduction in the validated clone: tags peel to 8.0.2 commit 5225f2e584d7eff969cd39ca26aa67e5dd828736 and 8.0.3 commit 00c8ff1c98b5a1fabfc4c8e922d9bd7398908c77. 'git merge-base --is-ancestor 8577a9d602ad76354c3625673979038848aa3142 8.0.2' exits 1, while the same command against 8.0.3 exits 0; 'git merge-base --is-ancestor 6cab4ce3aad9bc65b52bc761a4aa88634a2bd0aa 8.0.3' also exits 0. This matches the first-party 8.0.3 fixed boundary.

reasoning: The weakness is not bad password comparison; it is the absence of any control around repeated failures. The first authenticated remote REST wrapper is therefore the causal origin: it creates the exact repeatable challenge/failure loop and writes the vulnerable failure behavior, while its direct parent has no authenticated failed-attempt path. Later authenticator rewrites, module moves, the 2018 Eclipse snapshot import, and the 2026 merge are not introducers. Public predecessor history permits decomposition of the Eclipse root aggregate to the 2009 commit. The 2026 direct fix places one tracker around the shared administrator authentication path, covering REST and the Console's REST-backed login, and 8.0.3 is the first release containing the completed fix series. Because the BIC commit object is a 2009 human-authored commit with no AI marker, the only supported closed verdict is NOT_AI.
